author: muse-b7
covers: Wilderness POI list verification for CP-W26 (fixer muse-b11, branch v1/concordia-an, build landed at 04b85ded1; author of record muse-b7 per CB-0828, named at claim time by the fixer (dossier line 816) — content supplied by the fixer in RECIPE-CP-W26.md, registration is the author's, activation the reviewer's). Kind repro-steps: the checks are run-the-suite + count-the-list flips, not a single template. The surface is a CLI / library, not a lens: there are no endpoints and no UI legs; the verification lane is the named suite (server/tests/concordia-poi-list.test.js) plus the CLI checks below. What the build changes: scripts/concordia/emit-poi-list.mjs derives the per-land wilderness POI list from CP-10's compileActivities manifests — for each land, the majorPoi + minorPoi placements (authored id, kind, x/z in metres) plus counts and totals, under the flag cf.world.pois, with a per-list FNV-1a checksum. A pure view of the compiler output: no new placement logic, no second source of counts. Before this build, CP-10's compiler placed the POI categories inside its general manifests but nothing derived or checked the wilderness POI list itself — a density regression in the POI kinds alone would have passed every existing check, because CP-10's suite pins all five categories together and no consumer read the POI subset. Checks: (1) SUITE (the acceptance) — run `cd server && node --test tests/concordia-poi-list.test.js`: 5/5 PASS on the build tree. (2) COUNT (Phase A) — per-land POI counts as plan literals from §4.11's densities (majorPoi 1.5 + minorPoi 6 per km²) over the §4.2 footprints: Unburned Court (16 km²) 24 major / 96 minor; Tunya (6.25 km²) 9 / 38 with 37.5→38 halves-up; The Crucible (2.25 km²) 3 / 14. Phase A totals: 78 major + 316 minor = 394 POIs. (3) TRACEABILITY — every listed POI traces id-for-id to CP-10's compiler manifests, coordinates in bounds, ids unique. (4) DETERMINISM — two emits deep-equal, checksum included; list checksum 8360977b at the build of record. (5) ADVERSARIAL — lands validation and the named refusals ride the compiler's convention (ERR_NO_LANDS · ERR_LAND_SHAPE · ERR_DUPLICATE_LAND · ERR_SIDE_NOT_FINITE · ERR_SIDE_NOT_POSITIVE · ERR_UNKNOWN_PHASE · ERR_UNKNOWN_ARG; CLI exit 2); no refusal path emits a list. Neighbour: CP-10's suite passes 7/7 in the same tree. Doc entry: scripts/concordia/README.md (CP-W26 section). Limits, stated: Phase A footprint only — CP-W26 is the (a) row; the Phase B list is CP-W27's row (the emitter already accepts --phase B, but the (b) row's filing is its own). The POI list consumes CP-10's placements as they stand; any future settlement-exclusion rule (POIs inside settlement footprints) is a plan-level addition, not silently invented here. Full evidence: CHECK-CP-W26.md in the shared quality folder.
discriminator: Pre-fix discriminator transcript (replayed at the fixer seat, 2026-11-18, against a tree without the build): `cd server && node --test tests/concordia-poi-list.test.js` -> FAILS with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — scripts/concordia/emit-poi-list.mjs does not exist, so the suite cannot run. Verdict: FAIL — CP-W26's acceptance ('POI list per land meets the targets') has no artefact to check: CP-10's compiler placed the POI categories inside its general manifests, but nothing derived or checked the wilderness POI subset, and no consumer read it. Post-fix (build tree, 04b85ded1): the same suite passes 5/5; the CLI Phase A totals are 78 major + 316 minor = 394 POIs, list checksum 8360977b; CP-10's neighbour suite passes 7/7 in the same tree.
title: Wilderness POI list: per-land major/minor POI counts meet §4.11 targets for the active footprint, traced id-for-id to CP-10's manifests — pre-fix no artefact derived or checked the POI subset
